clue.text: Island race — runs it in error

indicators.note: in tells us the two short pieces go inside the word for a mistake

parts.note: bish is ... slang for a blunder or mistake
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a whole island nation of running things badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' looks like a comment on the race; error is British slang 'bish'. 'Island race' is the definition, not a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of an island nation in Europe are collectively called by this adjective-turned-noun.

clue.text: Cheerfully endure speculator having success

parts.note: a bear is a stock-market speculator who bets on falling prices
up means ahead or winning, as in 'two goals up'

explanation.surface: A trader on the exchange copes well with having done well.
explanation.walkthrough: A bear sells shares expecting prices to fall; 'having' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to stay brave and cope with hardship.

clue.text: Continentals are not so narrow-minded

parts.note: people from mainland Europe, unlike islanders, are said not to have an island mentality

explanation.surface: Mainland Europeans claim to be more open than some.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'continental' is the opposite of 'island', so an islander's outlook is the narrow one.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally relating to an island, it has come to mean parochial and closed to outside ideas.

clue.text: All the same, I make an impression on one state

parts.note: to dent is to make an impression in a surface
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of making their mark on a particular state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make an impression' sounds like gaining influence but means a physical dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Things exactly alike in every respect are all the same.

clue.text: With head seen, kid may be discovered in this

definitions.text: With head seen, kid may be discovered in this

parts.words: With head seen, kid may be discovered in this
parts.note: a children's game in which a child poking their head out from cover gets found

explanation.surface: A goat kid is spotted when its head shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' suggests a young goat; it is a child playing a game of concealment and searching.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a children's game where one player looks for others who have concealed themselves.

clue.text: Classic route modern French artist follows

indicators.note: follows puts the artist's name after the road abbreviation

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a route through a town
Fernand Leger was a twentieth-century French painter

explanation.surface: A painter of the modern French school trails along a familiar road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Classics are the five great English flat horse races; this one is run at Doncaster. 'Classic' looks like an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This Doncaster horse race is one of the five British flat-racing Classics.

clue.text: Amount Marathon leader's up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the pieces to read from the bottom
leader picks out the opening letter of Marathon

parts.note: the apostrophe-s stands for 'us', as in let's for let us

explanation.surface: Someone asks how far ahead the leader of a marathon is.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M (Marathon's leader) and US (the 's of 'let's'), giving MUS, and 'up' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is an amount of money or figures added together.

clue.text: Man, for example, holding up line of fine thread

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means the island sits beneath, supporting the line letter

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island

explanation.surface: A man is holding up a strand of fine thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine smooth cotton thread used for stockings, named after the French town Lille.

clue.text: English king a European upset in island

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, stands for King George, an English monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down so they read upwards

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: An English monarch and a Continental fall out on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: GR (Georgius Rex) is a royal cipher for King George. 'upset' turns A DANE into ENADA.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean country in the Windward group is known as the spice isle.

clue.text: Trial for motorist — Toad crashing into others

indicators.note: into places the scrambled word inside the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: crashing suggests the letters of Toad are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Mr Toad, the reckless driver, smashes into other cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' makes OADT from the clue's Toad, after Toad of Toad Hall, the reckless motorist in The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial drive of a vehicle to check its performance is a test on the road.

clue.text: Cockney's pet mother found in port

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so a hamster becomes 'amster
dam is a mother, chiefly of animals

explanation.surface: A Londoner's hamster and its mother turn up at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are East Londoners noted for dropping the initial H, so the pet loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital is a major seaport on the IJ inlet.

clue.text: Italian city needing: another.. name when burnt

definitions.text: Italian city needing: another.. name when burnt

parts.words: Italian city needing: another.. name when burnt
parts.note: a Tuscan city's name plus one more N (for name) gives the earth pigment sold as 'burnt' brown

explanation.surface: A city in Italy must be renamed after a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Burnt sienna is a brown pigment spelt with a double N; the Tuscan city has one, so it needs 'another name' (N = name) to become the paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan hill city famous for its Palio horse race gives its name to an earth pigment.

clue.text: In which a Frenchman sleeps in the dark

definitions.meaning: ... is French for 'a bed', the thing a Frenchman sleeps in

explanation.surface: A Frenchman sleeps somewhere without the lights on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two French words, the letters give 'un lit', 'a bed'; read as one English word they mean lacking light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no lamps burning leaves you without light, sitting in darkness.

clue.text: Play written by Shaw as a vehicle for Jonathan and others

definitions.meaning: The ... is a 1928 political comedy by George Bernard Shaw

definitions.text: a vehicle for Jonathan and others
definitions.meaning: Jonathan is a variety of eating apple, so a barrow for carrying fruit

explanation.surface: A Shaw play is being staged as a showcase for a lead actor called Jonathan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' suggests a star part for an actor; Jonathan is in fact an apple variety, and the vehicle is a literal cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's comedy title and a barrow for fruit share this name.

clue.text: Survive bad piece of driving run into however

parts.note: a pull is a golf drive hooked off line

indicators.note: into puts the run letter inside the word for however

parts.note: though means however
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A motorist does a poor bit of driving and runs into trouble but survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' suggests a car, but in golf a pull is a badly hit drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover from illness or hardship is to come out the other side alive.

clue.text: Line of children hurries along, showing insincere grief

parts.note: in Britain a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
to tear is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: A file of schoolchildren rushes off while someone fakes sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is the British name for a column of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from the myth that the reptile weeps while eating its prey, hence feigned sorrow.

clue.text: Money the first bidder offered for ' kitchen equipment

parts.note: tin is British slang for money
in bridge the opener is the player who makes the first bid

explanation.surface: At an auction, cash is offered for a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bidder' suggests an auction; in bridge the first player to bid is the opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand tool for cutting the lids off cans is standard kitchen gear.

clue.text: Source of divine music Peter, transmits

parts.note: Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up
pipes means sends along, as in piping music

explanation.surface: Someone called Peter broadcasts heavenly music.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek god Pan played these reed pipes, making them divine music.
explanation.definitionFit: The reed instrument played by the god Pan produces music fit for a deity.

clue.text: A very raw point on part of one's leg

parts.note: raw weather is chilly, and very chilly is the superlative
an end is a point or tip
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sore spot somewhere on the leg is causing pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very raw' reads as sore but means coldest, giving the superlative form. 'A very raw point' is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This cord joining the calf muscle to the heel bone is part of the lower limb.

clue.text: Alternative for the acre

indicators.note: Alternative signals another arrangement of the letters of the acre

explanation.surface: A metric measure is suggested as a replacement for an imperial unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative' rearranges THE ACRE; the whole clue also defines the metric land unit used in place of the acre.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of land, 10,000 square metres, replaces the older imperial measure.

clue.text: Outstanding bowling? Exactly

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
due means exactly, as in due north

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator praises some fine bowling as spot on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests excellent but means unpaid or late.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill still unpaid after its date is outstanding.

clue.text: Bishop blessing dog

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an asset is a boon or blessing

explanation.surface: A bishop gives a blessing to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short-legged hound breed with long ears.

clue.text: Controller of vital beat who sets speed limits?

definitions.meaning: an implanted device regulating the rhythm of the heart
a runner who sets the tempo in a race for others to follow

explanation.surface: A heart device is pictured as a traffic official setting speed limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cardiac implant and a runner who dictates the pace of a race.

clue.text: Gong bringing many into dinner, -perhaps

indicators.note: into puts the Roman numeral inside the word for dinner

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A gong is struck to bring a crowd in to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong summons people to dinner, but here it is slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a decoration or award given for honour.

clue.text: By Mondrian, a sacred work of art

parts.note: Piet Mondrian was the Dutch abstract painter

explanation.surface: A religious artwork is attributed to the abstract painter Mondrian.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname is the misleading part; only Mondrian's first name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, a devotional image.

clue.text: Patterned cloth put on piano'

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the word for put after the music letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
laid means put or placed

explanation.surface: A patterned fabric has been draped over a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan twill cloth, woven in checks, is the Scottish fabric meant.

clue.text: Steak done badly in French place

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the French town

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France

indicators.note: badly says the letters of done are poorly arranged

explanation.surface: A steak has been overcooked in a French restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes NEDO. 'French place' is the Loire city, not a generic spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small round cut of beef fillet, a classic French dish.

clue.text: Essay of 15 lines

definitions.meaning: a score made over the line by a rugby union team of fifteen

explanation.surface: A school essay is limited to fifteen lines.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby union side has fifteen players, and a touchdown over the opponents' line scores this.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, and a rugby score over the goal line shares the same word.

clue.text: One English poet's bashful about Parisienne…

indicators.note: about means the shy word goes round the French pronoun

parts.note: shy means bashful
elle is French for 'she', so a Parisian woman

explanation.surface: A Romantic poet is coy in the presence of a Parisian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisienne' stands for a woman of Paris, so the French word for 'she'.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe, the Romantic who wrote 'Ozymandias', bore this surname.

clue.text: … while another's in her bed endlessly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the word for a bed

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a second poet is tucked up in a woman's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' carries on from 26 Across: another English poet, George Herbert. 'endlessly' cuts BERTH to BERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Following on from the previous clue, it means a second English poet: George, the seventeenth-century metaphysical writer.
